M0: spec first — normative SPEC.md and the golden conformance suite

The proposal calls for the specification to enter the repository before any
code, because two implementations (this Python engine and an internal Java
one) must be held to one source of truth.

- spec/SPEC.md: the nine principles (P1-P9) and ten invariants (INV-1..INV-10)
  written normatively, plus the exact assertion_id derivation, projection
  algorithm, conflict-resolution order, retract guards and query semantics.
- spec/conformance/: language-neutral golden YAML cases. Every case is also
  replayed and re-ingested by the runner, so INV-2 (idempotent replay) and
  INV-3 (projection is a pure, rebuildable function) are enforced for free on
  every case rather than tested once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M1: deterministic engine core, SQLite store, query family and CLI

Card-level ingest -> assertions -> intervals -> materialized memory cards,
with the read path deriving answers by query alone (P4/INV-10).

Design decisions worth calling out, each traceable to a production bug the
proposal records:

- INV-4 (blocker/next_step/due flicker): a field being absent means "no
  observation", never "cleared"; explicit clearing is expressed by
  EpisodeCard.cleared_fields. The condition that emits a RETRACT and the
  condition that updates the projection are one shared function, not two
  copies that can drift, and re-asserting the same value keeps the existing
  interval open instead of closing and reopening it.
- INV-5 (two unrelated matters merged into one card): merging requires an
  absolute floor of two shared sources; a single shared message is never a
  merge reason, no matter what share of the new card's evidence it represents.
- INV-8/INV-9: SINGLE conflicts resolve on (valid_from, origin, recorded_at,
  assertion_id) with human origin outranking model, and every resolved
  conflict is counted and reported rather than silently discarded.

The core carries no domain vocabulary: it executes any valid SchemaProfile,
and ships two genuinely different profiles (org-matters, personal-decisions)
so the abstraction is driven by more than one case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M2+M3: distillation gate, protocol surfaces, adapters, PostgreSQL and release

Write path (the only place a model is allowed to run, P1):
- LlmGateway SPI (OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / null) behind an async dream
  queue. ingest() never calls a model; dream() drains the queue and re-projects
  inside one transaction (INV-6).
- A validation gate with named, counted rejection reasons (P3). The load-bearing
  one is SOURCE_NOT_TRACEABLE: a candidate's cited sources must be a subset of
  the originating card's evidence, so the model cannot invent provenance. The
  same traceability check backs the message->card adapter — one implementation,
  not two.
- Gated creation of non-primary child subjects, which is what makes the
  flagship profile's one semantic predicate (decision_adopted on DECISION_SLOT)
  reachable at all. Child keys are derived deterministically, so a replayed
  dream creates no duplicate subject.

Read path: MCP server on the official SDK (seven tools), FastAPI REST 1:1 with
those tools, and a Claude Skill. All three share one service layer, and none of
them can reach the distill package — enforced by an import-graph test.

Storage: a second backend. PostgreSQL exists to prove the spec is implementable
twice, so the entire conformance suite runs against both, and ordering is
pinned to bytewise (COLLATE "C" / BINARY) rather than the server's locale — a
spec whose answers depend on a deployment's collation is not a spec.

Release: adapters for ReMe/OpenViking digests, four runnable examples including
the human-correction flow, Docker, docs, and CI with the cross-backend
conformance suite as a required gate against the two implementations drifting.

Verified: 138 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17, on both C and
en_US.UTF-8 collations; mh conformance run passes 37/37 on both backends and
exits non-zero on a seeded failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cli): honest exit-code contract and a terminal correction path

Both defects were masked by a fabricated dependency: a previous build could not
download Typer and installed a 103-line hand-written stub into the venv under
the name `typer 0.0.0+verification`. Every CLI test had been passing against
that stub. The venv has been rebuilt with real Typer 0.27.0, which is how these
surfaced.

- `mh conformance run` now exits 0 when all cases pass, 1 when cases run and
  some fail, and 2 when the suite itself is unusable. It previously raised
  click.exceptions.Exit(2), which the stub honoured and real Typer does not, so
  an unreadable suite exited 1 with a traceback. This command is the CI gate and
  the harness the internal Java implementation mirrors, so its exit contract is
  part of the deliverable, not an implementation detail.
- `mh correct` closes the one surface where the correction protocol was missing.
  P8 makes corrections a first-class part of the core contract and the proposal
  names an unused correction protocol as a top risk, yet an operator at a
  terminal had no way to file one.
- Typer and click now carry lower bounds so a fresh install cannot silently
  pick up an incompatible version.

Verified: 141 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; the three exit codes
demonstrated for real; a correction through the CLI flips a query answer from
(blocked, model) to (open, human).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: hands-on acceptance manual

A step-by-step guide for verifying the engine by running it rather than by
reading the code or trusting test names. Every command and every expected
output in it was executed on a clean venv before being written down.

It walks the invariants that came from production bugs — the blocker flicker
(INV-4), the two-matters-merged-into-one card (INV-5), human precedence
(INV-9), zero-LLM reads (INV-10) — and shows what a broken result looks like,
not only a passing one. It also records the eight places where the proposal was
ambiguous and a judgement call was made, so those can be overruled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: assert CLI contracts, not rendered layout

The third environment-dependent failure in this suite. CI failed on all three
Python versions because a test asserted that '--backend' appears in Rich's
rendered help output; at 80 columns Rich wraps the flag across lines and the
substring is simply not there. Reproduced locally with COLUMNS=60.

The tests now normalise help output before asserting, so they check that the
CLI documents its contract rather than checking how Rich happened to lay it
out. CONTRIBUTING.md now states the rule, since this class of defect has now
cost three rounds: tests must not assert on rendered layout, machine-specific
paths, or anything else that varies with the runner's environment.

Verified: 104 passed both in a wide terminal and under
COLUMNS=60 NO_COLOR=1 TERM=dumb; ruff still exits 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M4: ingest from communication data — Record layer, Slack adapter, evidence lifecycle

The engine's goal is memory over a team's real communication; until now the
only entry was a pre-built EpisodeCard. This milestone adds the layer below.

- Record contract generalizes ChatMessage: container/thread identity, author
  kind, permalink, reactions, edit and revocation timestamps. record_id is
  namespaced (container:native_id) and validated — Slack's ts is unique only
  within a channel, and two channels' identical timestamps collapsing into one
  source_id would corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count and merge unrelated
  matters. A golden case now proves cross-channel same-ts is never shared
  evidence.
- INV-11 (new, normative): an edited source is a new observation — a new
  assertion alongside the old one, distinguishable by recorded_at; a deleted
  source revokes evidence — no assertion or interval is removed, but query
  results carry evidence_status so a conclusion resting on revoked evidence is
  visibly flagged instead of silently persisting or vanishing. SourceRef
  gains uri so P5's promise ends at a clickable permalink.
- Slack adapter (pure, no LLM): conversations.history and message events to
  Records — mrkdwn unescaping and entity resolution, Block Kit, bot vs human
  authors, thread identity, permalink construction, non-conversational
  subtypes filtered so they never become evidence.
- Thread-first identity: a thread is the default matter boundary; cross-thread
  merging still requires the INV-5 evidence floor.
- Wired in: engine.add_records, mh extract, MCP add_records (8 tools), REST
  /v1/add_records, with per-container sync watermarks. Re-syncing an
  overlapping window is a complete no-op and does not re-invoke the model.

Verified: 159 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17 (40 golden cases);
narrow-terminal run green; ruff clean; the Slack fixture example runs end to
end with readable excerpts and clickable evidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M5: the two-verb facade — add(messages) and matters()

The project brief's §15.4 names the north star: mem0 won developers with two
verbs; ours are add and matters. Until now the outer door was the card-level
contract — the engine's internal promise boundary, not a user's entry point.

- engine.add(scope_id, messages): minimal four-field contract
  {id, sender{id,name}, text, sent_at} — exactly the gate's three requirements
  (traceability / time / participant), so the easy door does not weaken P5.
  Message ids are namespaced internally (scope:conversation:id) so colliding
  ids across conversations cannot corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count.
- Receipts: add returns {accepted, task_id} immediately and never calls the
  LLM inline (P1); flush/wait runs the pipeline; engine.task() exposes status,
  cards produced, new assertions, and the gate's rejection breakdown by reason
  — observability none of the L1 tools offer. Tasks persist in both stores.
- engine.matters() returns ergonomic projected objects (.title .status .owners
  .blocked_by .next_step ...) — zero LLM, straight from the projection.
- Protocol surfaces made isomorphic and resource-style: POST
  /v1/scopes/{id}/messages|cards, GET matters, GET query/*, POST corrections,
  GET /v1/tasks/{id}; MCP gains add_messages (9 tools); CLI gains
  mh add / mh matters / mh flush / mh task, with mh init scaffolding a config
  and an offline fixture demo. Old RPC routes removed — no released users.
- Quiet-period auto-flush in service mode only; embedded stays host-driven.
- ingest renamed add_cards (deprecated alias kept); add_records demoted to
  the advanced layer. README (EN/zh) leads with the five-minute journey; SPEC
  gains the §15.1 admission test as a normative rule, the message contract,
  and receipt semantics; 43 golden cases.

Verified: 174 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; narrow-terminal
green; ruff clean; the journey run end to end in a temp dir as a new user;
colliding-id and gate-breakdown probes pass; MCP add_messages called over the
real protocol.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M6: the asset becomes a trigger — events, export/import, daily flush

Completes the output surfaces of the brief's §15.2: every output keeps the
three properties (traceable / replayable / deterministic).

- Change events are DERIVED FROM PROJECTION DIFFS, never a second write path:
  after each rebuild the previous interval set is diffed against the new one.
  Assertions stay the only source of truth (P7); events are reproducible
  artifacts with deterministic event_ids, so replay() — which rebuilds the
  same intervals — emits zero new events (P9). Types: matter_created,
  status_changed(from/to), matter_completed, blocked/unblocked,
  decision_adopted, value_corrected; every event carries origin and
  source_ids, so a human correction is visible as origin=human in the stream.
  Queryable (engine.events / GET /v1/scopes/{id}/events / mh events) and
  pushable (mh serve --webhook-url, at-least-once with bounded backoff,
  consumers dedupe by event_id).
- Export/import: mh export produces a versioned, self-contained envelope
  (profile, subjects, assertions — the asset); mh import into an empty store
  reproduces byte-identical projections and query answers, corrections
  surviving with origin intact. Ownership of the memory asset is a deliverable,
  not a promise.
- Service mode gains daily_flush_at alongside the quiet-period loop; embedded
  stays host-driven.
- M5 acceptance defects fixed: unknown task/scope/subject return structured
  404s instead of tracebacks; synchronous wait=true responses now carry
  task_id.

Verified: 190 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17 (47 golden cases);
narrow-terminal green; ruff clean; journey -> correction -> events -> export ->
import -> replay round trip run by hand with identical results and a stable
event count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ledger phase 1: GitHub adapter, devlog, repeatable fill

Groundwork for the self-hosted ledger — matterhorn maintaining its own
development ledger as the project's flagship demo. The design splits into a
nightly CI write path (LLM distills the repo's own history into assertions,
committed back) and a zero-LLM read path (anyone clones, imports the
committed assertions, and reproduces the identical ledger — the zero-model
and pure-projection invariants as a public, hands-on fact).

- adapters/github.py: git log (NUL-delimited pretty format) and GitHub
  issues/PR comments to Records, style-aligned with the Slack adapter. Every
  piece of evidence carries a public clickable URL (commit or issue html_url);
  author identity is stable across commits; empty issue lists are first-class
  since this repo has none yet.
- devlog/0001-project-strategy.md: the decision-semantics source, written
  strictly from the repo's public documents with per-section source links —
  nothing invented. Its GitHub URL becomes the source_ref for the devlog
  message.
- scripts/ledger_fill.py: the repeatable fill — git history + devlog
  (+ issues via gh api) -> add -> flush against ledger/dev.db (gitignored).
  Real credentials come from the environment; without one it refuses before
  ingesting rather than silently falling back to fixtures. Verified: a second
  run over the same history processes zero records (P9).

Verified: 197 tests total green, ruff clean, conformance unchanged at 47.
The real LLM first fill and the human quality review of the resulting matters
are the next step, gated on a credential.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ledger phase 2: the project ledgers itself

The self-hosted ledger goes live: MATTERS.md at the repo root is generated
from assertions distilled out of this repository's own history, and anyone
can reproduce it without an LLM key:

  mh import ledger/assertions.json --db ledger/dev.db && mh matters dev

- Extraction robustness, motivated by live runs: prompts now assign each
  message a short alias (m1, m2, ...) and the extractor maps citations back
  to real record ids deterministically — the gate contract is untouched, and
  a qwen3:4b-class model that previously failed every citation now has a
  fair chance while fabricated aliases still die at the gate. Extraction is
  batched (thread-respecting) instead of one giant prompt per container.
- Provider portability, motivated by DeepSeek: response_format degrades
  json_schema -> json_object -> none on providers that reject strict schema
  (the gate is the real enforcement; the API-level schema is an optimization),
  and both prompts pin their output envelope with a literal example — losing
  server-side schema enforcement no longer lets a model invent envelope keys.
  MATTERHORN_TIMEOUT is formalized with validation and tests.
- mh export --format markdown renders matters with collapsible timelines,
  clickable evidence links, and visible [human correction] badges;
  deterministic byte-identical output from identical state.
- .github/workflows/ledger.yml: nightly + manual, rebuilds the projection
  from the committed assertion export, fills incrementally, commits only on
  change; credentials from secrets, fail-fast when absent.
- Ledger content from the first real fill (DeepSeek): 14 records -> 14 cards
  accepted by the gate -> 42 assertions -> 14 matters, every timeline entry
  linking to its commit. Verified: rebuild-from-export renders byte-identical
  MATTERS.md, and a no-new-commits nightly cycle produces zero diff.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ledger: break the self-feeding loop, pin batch size, refresh content

Two consecutive CI runs each produced a commit: run two ingested run one's
own 'ledger: nightly update' commit as development activity — the ledger was
ledgering its own bookkeeping, one new matter per night, never converging.
Bookkeeping commits (the github-actions bot author, or the workflow's fixed
message) are now deterministically excluded from ingestion, with tests.

Extraction batches default to five records: at eight, a live DeepSeek run
returned an empty card list for one whole batch — half the history silently
missing from the ledger with nothing in the drop reasons. Five-record batches
produced full coverage (15 records -> 15 gated cards -> 45 assertions).

Ledger content regenerated from the clean fill; every matter's timeline links
to its commit, and the reproduce loop (import committed assertions -> render)
remains byte-identical.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

console: readable conversation names for source labels

Source chips overflowed their cards and showed raw session UUIDs. A
conversation_names directory (both backends, person_names pattern) now
maps conversation keys to display names: Claude Code hooks derive a
session title from the first user message (cc:<first line>), dumbo IM
keys already carry the group name, and Message gains an optional
conversation_label so any connector can name its conversations. Labels
resolve at read time; unnamed keys shorten opaque uuid/hex segments,
and doubled X:X keys from prefix-embedding message ids collapse to the
conversation itself. Chips are clamped inside the card with ellipsis.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

console: conversation identity stays the key, names disambiguate

Display names never participate in identity: conversation_id (the
stable connector target) remains the only uniqueness key for
windowing, staging, and routing, and the dumbo forward script now
sends the target as conversation_id with the group name only in
conversation_label. On the read side, two different conversations
sharing one display name render with a short key-hash suffix so the
wall never looks merged when the data is not; matters and the detail
timeline map share the same disambiguation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

console: stale-page banner on UI redeploys

Open tabs poll data every five seconds but never reload their scripts,
so every UI redeploy left running pages silently stale - the recurring
"why didn't the display change" turned out to be old JavaScript more
than once. The page now records the server's asset version (a hash of
the console template, so restarts without UI changes never nag) on its
first poll and, when a later poll sees a different version, shows a
fixed banner offering a one-click reload.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

console: information architecture - focus wall, groups, ledger rows

The wall becomes an operating surface instead of a scope dump. Matters
render as full-width ledger rows - status stamp, title, one-line
progress summary, red blocker segment, source-conversation chips,
owner/due/next, update time - grouped into configurable project
sections ([console.groups] in matterhorn.toml, trailing-* patterns,
first match wins) with a Focus/All toggle: active matters (live
status, recent update, or pending action) sort by recency while the
rest folds into a per-group archive drawer. A Today strip surfaces
each group's latest changes. The detail dialog gains deterministic
cross-scope related matters via shared handles or title-token overlap.
Matter payloads now carry the projected progress value.

Also aligns the local lint gate with CI (ruff check src tests) and
clears the two violations that had main's CI red since yesterday.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

routing: candidates need real lexical kinship; new is the safe default

Acceptance audit of the 111-item review queue: eight of eight sampled
abstentions were serial duplicates of novel topics facing candidates
related by a single shared token - noise candidates manufacture the
dilemma, the adjudicator abstains, no matter forms, and the next
window repeats the loop. Recall now requires a token overlap of at
least two, and the adjudication prompt states plainly that new is the
confident answer for uncovered topics; abstention is reserved for
being genuinely torn between candidates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

engine: record change, not confirmation (change-only admission)

Every source type showed the same silt: models re-assert unchanged
values each extraction window - a matter collected status=in_progress
five times then completed three times, one email project logged nine
same-value confirmations, participants re-recorded twenty-one times.
Model-origin ASSERTs whose object_key is already live for the
predicate (SINGLE value equal, SET member present, APPEND point
identical) are now dropped at admission, counted as unchanged_dropped
in gate and task statistics. RETRACT, cleared_fields, and human-origin
assertions are exempt - a human repeating a value is an affirmation
with provenance. Timelines record change; staging keeps the dropped
evidence. Golden cases 02/27/28 updated to the intended semantics,
new cases 76-80 pin drop, change-after-drop, SET member, human
exemption, and replay identity on both backends.

Live five-window lifecycle now projects exactly two status entries
and four drops - previously five duplicates.

M0: spec first — normative SPEC.md and the golden conformance suite

The proposal calls for the specification to enter the repository before any
code, because two implementations (this Python engine and an internal Java
one) must be held to one source of truth.

- spec/SPEC.md: the nine principles (P1-P9) and ten invariants (INV-1..INV-10)
  written normatively, plus the exact assertion_id derivation, projection
  algorithm, conflict-resolution order, retract guards and query semantics.
- spec/conformance/: language-neutral golden YAML cases. Every case is also
  replayed and re-ingested by the runner, so INV-2 (idempotent replay) and
  INV-3 (projection is a pure, rebuildable function) are enforced for free on
  every case rather than tested once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M1: deterministic engine core, SQLite store, query family and CLI

Card-level ingest -> assertions -> intervals -> materialized memory cards,
with the read path deriving answers by query alone (P4/INV-10).

Design decisions worth calling out, each traceable to a production bug the
proposal records:

- INV-4 (blocker/next_step/due flicker): a field being absent means "no
  observation", never "cleared"; explicit clearing is expressed by
  EpisodeCard.cleared_fields. The condition that emits a RETRACT and the
  condition that updates the projection are one shared function, not two
  copies that can drift, and re-asserting the same value keeps the existing
  interval open instead of closing and reopening it.
- INV-5 (two unrelated matters merged into one card): merging requires an
  absolute floor of two shared sources; a single shared message is never a
  merge reason, no matter what share of the new card's evidence it represents.
- INV-8/INV-9: SINGLE conflicts resolve on (valid_from, origin, recorded_at,
  assertion_id) with human origin outranking model, and every resolved
  conflict is counted and reported rather than silently discarded.

The core carries no domain vocabulary: it executes any valid SchemaProfile,
and ships two genuinely different profiles (org-matters, personal-decisions)
so the abstraction is driven by more than one case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M2+M3: distillation gate, protocol surfaces, adapters, PostgreSQL and release

Write path (the only place a model is allowed to run, P1):
- LlmGateway SPI (OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / null) behind an async dream
  queue. ingest() never calls a model; dream() drains the queue and re-projects
  inside one transaction (INV-6).
- A validation gate with named, counted rejection reasons (P3). The load-bearing
  one is SOURCE_NOT_TRACEABLE: a candidate's cited sources must be a subset of
  the originating card's evidence, so the model cannot invent provenance. The
  same traceability check backs the message->card adapter — one implementation,
  not two.
- Gated creation of non-primary child subjects, which is what makes the
  flagship profile's one semantic predicate (decision_adopted on DECISION_SLOT)
  reachable at all. Child keys are derived deterministically, so a replayed
  dream creates no duplicate subject.

Read path: MCP server on the official SDK (seven tools), FastAPI REST 1:1 with
those tools, and a Claude Skill. All three share one service layer, and none of
them can reach the distill package — enforced by an import-graph test.

Storage: a second backend. PostgreSQL exists to prove the spec is implementable
twice, so the entire conformance suite runs against both, and ordering is
pinned to bytewise (COLLATE "C" / BINARY) rather than the server's locale — a
spec whose answers depend on a deployment's collation is not a spec.

Release: adapters for ReMe/OpenViking digests, four runnable examples including
the human-correction flow, Docker, docs, and CI with the cross-backend
conformance suite as a required gate against the two implementations drifting.

Verified: 138 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17, on both C and
en_US.UTF-8 collations; mh conformance run passes 37/37 on both backends and
exits non-zero on a seeded failure.

fix(cli): honest exit-code contract and a terminal correction path

Both defects were masked by a fabricated dependency: a previous build could not
download Typer and installed a 103-line hand-written stub into the venv under
the name `typer 0.0.0+verification`. Every CLI test had been passing against
that stub. The venv has been rebuilt with real Typer 0.27.0, which is how these
surfaced.

- `mh conformance run` now exits 0 when all cases pass, 1 when cases run and
  some fail, and 2 when the suite itself is unusable. It previously raised
  click.exceptions.Exit(2), which the stub honoured and real Typer does not, so
  an unreadable suite exited 1 with a traceback. This command is the CI gate and
  the harness the internal Java implementation mirrors, so its exit contract is
  part of the deliverable, not an implementation detail.
- `mh correct` closes the one surface where the correction protocol was missing.
  P8 makes corrections a first-class part of the core contract and the proposal
  names an unused correction protocol as a top risk, yet an operator at a
  terminal had no way to file one.
- Typer and click now carry lower bounds so a fresh install cannot silently
  pick up an incompatible version.

Verified: 141 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; the three exit codes
demonstrated for real; a correction through the CLI flips a query answer from
(blocked, model) to (open, human).

docs: hands-on acceptance manual

A step-by-step guide for verifying the engine by running it rather than by
reading the code or trusting test names. Every command and every expected
output in it was executed on a clean venv before being written down.

It walks the invariants that came from production bugs — the blocker flicker
(INV-4), the two-matters-merged-into-one card (INV-5), human precedence
(INV-9), zero-LLM reads (INV-10) — and shows what a broken result looks like,
not only a passing one. It also records the eight places where the proposal was
ambiguous and a judgement call was made, so those can be overruled.

test: assert CLI contracts, not rendered layout

The third environment-dependent failure in this suite. CI failed on all three
Python versions because a test asserted that '--backend' appears in Rich's
rendered help output; at 80 columns Rich wraps the flag across lines and the
substring is simply not there. Reproduced locally with COLUMNS=60.

The tests now normalise help output before asserting, so they check that the
CLI documents its contract rather than checking how Rich happened to lay it
out. CONTRIBUTING.md now states the rule, since this class of defect has now
cost three rounds: tests must not assert on rendered layout, machine-specific

Verified: 104 passed both in a wide terminal and under
COLUMNS=60 NO_COLOR=1 TERM=dumb; ruff still exits 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M4: ingest from communication data — Record layer, Slack adapter, evidence lifecycle

The engine's goal is memory over a team's real communication; until now the
only entry was a pre-built EpisodeCard. This milestone adds the layer below.

- Record contract generalizes ChatMessage: container/thread identity, author
  kind, permalink, reactions, edit and revocation timestamps. record_id is
  namespaced (container:native_id) and validated — Slack's ts is unique only
  within a channel, and two channels' identical timestamps collapsing into one
  source_id would corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count and merge unrelated
  matters. A golden case now proves cross-channel same-ts is never shared
  evidence.
- INV-11 (new, normative): an edited source is a new observation — a new
  assertion alongside the old one, distinguishable by recorded_at; a deleted
  source revokes evidence — no assertion or interval is removed, but query
  results carry evidence_status so a conclusion resting on revoked evidence is
  visibly flagged instead of silently persisting or vanishing. SourceRef
  gains uri so P5's promise ends at a clickable permalink.
- Slack adapter (pure, no LLM): conversations.history and message events to
  Records — mrkdwn unescaping and entity resolution, Block Kit, bot vs human
  authors, thread identity, permalink construction, non-conversational
  subtypes filtered so they never become evidence.
- Thread-first identity: a thread is the default matter boundary; cross-thread
  merging still requires the INV-5 evidence floor.
- Wired in: engine.add_records, mh extract, MCP add_records (8 tools), REST
  /v1/add_records, with per-container sync watermarks. Re-syncing an
  overlapping window is a complete no-op and does not re-invoke the model.

Verified: 159 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17 (40 golden cases);
narrow-terminal run green; ruff clean; the Slack fixture example runs end to
end with readable excerpts and clickable evidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M5: the two-verb facade — add(messages) and matters()

The project brief's §15.4 names the north star: mem0 won developers with two
verbs; ours are add and matters. Until now the outer door was the card-level
contract — the engine's internal promise boundary, not a user's entry point.

- engine.add(scope_id, messages): minimal four-field contract
  {id, sender{id,name}, text, sent_at} — exactly the gate's three requirements
  (traceability / time / participant), so the easy door does not weaken P5.
  Message ids are namespaced internally (scope:conversation:id) so colliding
  ids across conversations cannot corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count.
- Receipts: add returns {accepted, task_id} immediately and never calls the
  LLM inline (P1); flush/wait runs the pipeline; engine.task() exposes status,
  cards produced, new assertions, and the gate's rejection breakdown by reason
  — observability none of the L1 tools offer. Tasks persist in both stores.
- engine.matters() returns ergonomic projected objects (.title .status .owners
  .blocked_by .next_step ...) — zero LLM, straight from the projection.
- Protocol surfaces made isomorphic and resource-style: POST
  /v1/scopes/{id}/messages|cards, GET matters, GET query/*, POST corrections,
  GET /v1/tasks/{id}; MCP gains add_messages (9 tools); CLI gains
  mh add / mh matters / mh flush / mh task, with mh init scaffolding a config
  and an offline fixture demo. Old RPC routes removed — no released users.
- Quiet-period auto-flush in service mode only; embedded stays host-driven.
- ingest renamed add_cards (deprecated alias kept); add_records demoted to
  the advanced layer. README (EN/zh) leads with the five-minute journey; SPEC
  gains the §15.1 admission test as a normative rule, the message contract,
  and receipt semantics; 43 golden cases.

Verified: 174 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; narrow-terminal
green; ruff clean; the journey run end to end in a temp dir as a new user;
colliding-id and gate-breakdown probes pass; MCP add_messages called over the
real protocol.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M6: the asset becomes a trigger — events, export/import, daily flush

Completes the output surfaces of the brief's §15.2: every output keeps the
three properties (traceable / replayable / deterministic).

- Change events are DERIVED FROM PROJECTION DIFFS, never a second write path:
  after each rebuild the previous interval set is diffed against the new one.
  Assertions stay the only source of truth (P7); events are reproducible
  artifacts with deterministic event_ids, so replay() — which rebuilds the
  same intervals — emits zero new events (P9). Types: matter_created,
  status_changed(from/to), matter_completed, blocked/unblocked,
  decision_adopted, value_corrected; every event carries origin and
  source_ids, so a human correction is visible as origin=human in the stream.
  Queryable (engine.events / GET /v1/scopes/{id}/events / mh events) and
  pushable (mh serve --webhook-url, at-least-once with bounded backoff,
  consumers dedupe by event_id).
- Export/import: mh export produces a versioned, self-contained envelope
  (profile, subjects, assertions — the asset); mh import into an empty store
  reproduces byte-identical projections and query answers, corrections
  surviving with origin intact. Ownership of the memory asset is a deliverable,
  not a promise.
- Service mode gains daily_flush_at alongside the quiet-period loop; embedded
  stays host-driven.
- M5 acceptance defects fixed: unknown task/scope/subject return structured
  404s instead of tracebacks; synchronous wait=true responses now carry
  task_id.

Verified: 190 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17 (47 golden cases);
narrow-terminal green; ruff clean; journey -> correction -> events -> export ->
import -> replay round trip run by hand with identical results and a stable
event count.

ledger phase 1: GitHub adapter, devlog, repeatable fill

Groundwork for the self-hosted ledger — matterhorn maintaining its own
development ledger as the project's flagship demo. The design splits into a
nightly CI write path (LLM distills the repo's own history into assertions,
committed back) and a zero-LLM read path (anyone clones, imports the
committed assertions, and reproduces the identical ledger — the zero-model
and pure-projection invariants as a public, hands-on fact).

- adapters/github.py: git log (NUL-delimited pretty format) and GitHub
  issues/PR comments to Records, style-aligned with the Slack adapter. Every
  piece of evidence carries a public clickable URL (commit or issue html_url);
  author identity is stable across commits; empty issue lists are first-class
  since this repo has none yet.
- devlog/0001-project-strategy.md: the decision-semantics source, written
  strictly from the repo's public documents with per-section source links —
  nothing invented. Its GitHub URL becomes the source_ref for the devlog
  message.
- scripts/ledger_fill.py: the repeatable fill — git history + devlog
  (+ issues via gh api) -> add -> flush against ledger/dev.db (gitignored).
  Real credentials come from the environment; without one it refuses before
  ingesting rather than silently falling back to fixtures. Verified: a second
  run over the same history processes zero records (P9).

Verified: 197 tests total green, ruff clean, conformance unchanged at 47.
The real LLM first fill and the human quality review of the resulting matters
are the next step, gated on a credential.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ledger phase 2: the project ledgers itself

The self-hosted ledger goes live: MATTERS.md at the repo root is generated
from assertions distilled out of this repository's own history, and anyone
can reproduce it without an LLM key:

  mh import ledger/assertions.json --db ledger/dev.db && mh matters dev

- Extraction robustness, motivated by live runs: prompts now assign each
  message a short alias (m1, m2, ...) and the extractor maps citations back
  to real record ids deterministically — the gate contract is untouched, and
  a qwen3:4b-class model that previously failed every citation now has a
  fair chance while fabricated aliases still die at the gate. Extraction is
  batched (thread-respecting) instead of one giant prompt per container.
- Provider portability, motivated by DeepSeek: response_format degrades
  json_schema -> json_object -> none on providers that reject strict schema
  (the gate is the real enforcement; the API-level schema is an optimization),
  and both prompts pin their output envelope with a literal example — losing
  server-side schema enforcement no longer lets a model invent envelope keys.
  MATTERHORN_TIMEOUT is formalized with validation and tests.
- mh export --format markdown renders matters with collapsible timelines,
  clickable evidence links, and visible [human correction] badges;
  deterministic byte-identical output from identical state.
- .github/workflows/ledger.yml: nightly + manual, rebuilds the projection
  from the committed assertion export, fills incrementally, commits only on
  change; credentials from secrets, fail-fast when absent.
- Ledger content from the first real fill (DeepSeek): 14 records -> 14 cards
  accepted by the gate -> 42 assertions -> 14 matters, every timeline entry
  linking to its commit. Verified: rebuild-from-export renders byte-identical
  MATTERS.md, and a no-new-commits nightly cycle produces zero diff.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ledger: break the self-feeding loop, pin batch size, refresh content

Two consecutive CI runs each produced a commit: run two ingested run one's
own 'ledger: nightly update' commit as development activity — the ledger was
ledgering its own bookkeeping, one new matter per night, never converging.
Bookkeeping commits (the github-actions bot author, or the workflow's fixed
message) are now deterministically excluded from ingestion, with tests.

Extraction batches default to five records: at eight, a live DeepSeek run
returned an empty card list for one whole batch — half the history silently
missing from the ledger with nothing in the drop reasons. Five-record batches
produced full coverage (15 records -> 15 gated cards -> 45 assertions).

Ledger content regenerated from the clean fill; every matter's timeline links
to its commit, and the reproduce loop (import committed assertions -> render)
remains byte-identical.

console: the operating surface — browse, query, correct, feed, chat

mh console mounts a static REST client on the serve port: the product's
operator/developer/demo surface, peer to MCP/REST/CLI/SDK but itself only a
client of documented public endpoints — where the REST API lacked a
capability, the API grew (GET /v1/scopes on both stores; POST
/v1/scopes/{id}/ingest with server-side format detection for chat lines,
YAML/JSON messages, and raw email) rather than the console getting a back
door.

Five blocks arranged as the product's own pipeline — 1 produce (paste +
extract with visible gate breakdown, offline sample via the fixture provider),
2 memory (matters and detail; every current value carries a first-class
Correct affordance that files an origin=human assertion with traceable
source), 3 consume (a host-side tool-use chat whose only tools are the five
deterministic queries through the same service layer REST uses, evidence chips
under every answer; plus the query workbench with human/raw views). Without
an LLM key the chat hides and everything else works.

Live DeepSeek testing hardened the chat loop: invalid tool arguments return
to the model as tool results instead of failing the turn, hitting the
tool-call cap forces a final no-tools answer instead of an error, and tool
descriptions state that list_matters already carries current values so models
stop fishing per-predicate. A Postgres-only DISTINCT/COLLATE error in
list_scopes was caught by the dual-backend run.

The visual language is the ledger-paper direction chosen from three designed
candidates: double-rule masthead, ruled-paper feed, stamp badges, italic
correction links, red-ink human annotations; sepia dark variant; loopback
bind by default.

Verified: 202 tests green locally, 244 with PostgreSQL 17, narrow-terminal

# Project strategy

## Layer and promise boundary

Matterhorn is a deterministic, evidence-backed temporal memory layer for
agents. Messages enter on the write side; projected matters and their history
come from persisted evidence rather than generation at answer time. The project
positions this as an L3 layer that complements broad L1 capture and retrieval
tools: Matterhorn accepts traceable upstream material and adds closed
predicates, bi-temporal assertions, deterministic projection, replay, and
first-class human correction.

Sources:
[README — project description and promise boundary](../README.md#the-promise-boundary),
[Positioning alongside L1 memory tools](../docs/positioning.md),
[SPEC — principles](../spec/SPEC.md#1-principles).

## Name and package

The public distribution name is `matterhorn-memory` on PyPI. The Python import
name remains `matterhorn`, as shown by the SDK entry point
`from matterhorn import Engine`.

Source:
[README — installation and SDK entry point](../README.md#five-minute-journey).

## Two-verb facade

The default SDK facade is deliberately centered on two verbs:
`add(messages)` for writes and `matters(scope_id)` for reads. `add()` persists a
task without calling an LLM and `flush()` runs the queued write pipeline;
`matters()` is a deterministic projected read and never calls an LLM. Direct
card and Record ingestion, detailed temporal queries, and correction remain
progressively disclosed advanced surfaces.

Sources:
[README — Two-verb SDK](../README.md#two-verb-sdk),
[README — Progressive disclosure](../README.md#progressive-disclosure),
[CHANGELOG 0.5.0](../CHANGELOG.md#050---2026-07-29).

## Thread-first identity

A communication thread is the first deterministic matter boundary. Identity
does not depend on a model choosing a subject. Cross-thread evidence merging
still obeys the evidence threshold, including the absolute rule that a single
shared source never causes a merge.

Sources:
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29),
[SPEC — evidence-based identity merge](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants).

## Evidence revocation, not conclusion deletion

Edited Records append new observations and assertions. Deleting or revoking a
Record does not mutate or remove the immutable assertions, intervals, or
materializations it supported. Queries keep the conclusion visible while
marking each source as active or revoked and reporting aggregate evidence
status.

Sources:
[SPEC — INV-11 immutable source lifecycle](../spec/SPEC.md#2-invariants),
[CHANGELOG 0.4.0](../CHANGELOG.md#040---2026-07-29).

## Dual-backend conformance

SQLite and PostgreSQL implement the same Store boundary. Backend-specific SQL
and value normalization stay inside the Store layer, and a behavioral
difference between the two backends is a defect. Both backends run the same
language-neutral golden conformance cases. The current public suite contains
47 cases.

Sources:
[SPEC — PostgreSQL Store and consistency boundary](../spec/SPEC.md#19-postgresql-store-and-consistency-boundary),
[SPEC — Reference conformance harness](../spec/SPEC.md#20-reference-conformance-harness),
[README — conformance suite](../README.md#the-promise-boundary).

## Current milestone

The latest release listed in the changelog is 0.6.0, dated 2026-07-29. It adds
deterministic projection-diff events, at-least-once webhook delivery, versioned
scope export/import, service-only daily UTC flushing, and four output-surface
conformance cases that bring the suite to 47.

Source:
[CHANGELOG 0.6.0](../CHANGELOG.md#060---2026-07-29).

fix(cli): honest exit-code contract and a terminal correction path

Both defects were masked by a fabricated dependency: a previous build could not
download Typer and installed a 103-line hand-written stub into the venv under
the name `typer 0.0.0+verification`. Every CLI test had been passing against
that stub. The venv has been rebuilt with real Typer 0.27.0, which is how these
surfaced.

- `mh conformance run` now exits 0 when all cases pass, 1 when cases run and
  some fail, and 2 when the suite itself is unusable. It previously raised
  click.exceptions.Exit(2), which the stub honoured and real Typer does not, so
  an unreadable suite exited 1 with a traceback. This command is the CI gate and
  the harness the internal Java implementation mirrors, so its exit contract is
  part of the deliverable, not an implementation detail.
- `mh correct` closes the one surface where the correction protocol was missing.
  P8 makes corrections a first-class part of the core contract and the proposal
  names an unused correction protocol as a top risk, yet an operator at a
  terminal had no way to file one.
- Typer and click now carry lower bounds so a fresh install cannot silently
  pick up an incompatible version.

Verified: 141 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; the three exit codes
demonstrated for real; a correction through the CLI flips a query answer from
(blocked, model) to (open, human).

M4: ingest from communication data — Record layer, Slack adapter, evidence lifecycle

The engine's goal is memory over a team's real communication; until now the
only entry was a pre-built EpisodeCard. This milestone adds the layer below.

- Record contract generalizes ChatMessage: container/thread identity, author
  kind, permalink, reactions, edit and revocation timestamps. record_id is
  namespaced (container:native_id) and validated — Slack's ts is unique only
  within a channel, and two channels' identical timestamps collapsing into one
  source_id would corrupt INV-5's shared-evidence count and merge unrelated
  matters. A golden case now proves cross-channel same-ts is never shared
  evidence.
- INV-11 (new, normative): an edited source is a new observation — a new
  assertion alongside the old one, distinguishable by recorded_at; a deleted
  source revokes evidence — no assertion or interval is removed, but query
  results carry evidence_status so a conclusion resting on revoked evidence is
  visibly flagged instead of silently persisting or vanishing. SourceRef
  gains uri so P5's promise ends at a clickable permalink.
- Slack adapter (pure, no LLM): conversations.history and message events to
  Records — mrkdwn unescaping and entity resolution, Block Kit, bot vs human
  authors, thread identity, permalink construction, non-conversational
  subtypes filtered so they never become evidence.
- Thread-first identity: a thread is the default matter boundary; cross-thread
  merging still requires the INV-5 evidence floor.
- Wired in: engine.add_records, mh extract, MCP add_records (8 tools), REST
  /v1/add_records, with per-container sync watermarks. Re-syncing an
  overlapping window is a complete no-op and does not re-invoke the model.

end with readable excerpts and clickable evidence.

console: readable matter timeline

Timeline entries now carry a conversation chip derived from the
evidence source id, so a matter fed by several sessions shows which
conversation each step came from; repeated chips dim to group
consecutive same-conversation entries. Long excerpts and values render
clamped (two and four lines) and toggle to full text on click instead

engine: clamp task newest_message_at to arrival time

A future-stamped message (source clock skew - hook events carry
timestamps from other machines) set a scope's newest_message_at ahead
of the server clock, and the quiet-period selector then considered the
scope永not-quiet, freezing its distillation until that future instant.
Enqueue now clamps newest_message_at to the task's created_at: skewed
messages count as arrived now, while genuinely old timestamps keep
flushing backfills immediately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject handles: identity becomes a searchable asset (refactor phase 1)

Subjects gain a typed handle registry. Bindings are evidenced,
revocable rows in subject_handles - at most one active owner per
(scope, type, normalized value), enforced by a partial unique index on
both backends. Handle recognition lives in SchemaProfile
handle_patterns, not code; org-matters/v1 ships conservative defaults
(issue keys, PR refs, keyword-prefixed order/invoice numbers, flight
numbers, Message-ID/thread ids) with the entropy rule pinned in SPEC:
bare numbers, amounts, and names must never be routing keys.

Ingestion scans accepted cards' cited records deterministically - zero
model - and binds matches to the resolved canonical subject; a value
already owned by another subject is observed and counted
(handle_conflicts), never rebound. Merges union handles by transparent
canonicalization so unmerge restores original ownership and replay
reproduces the binding state (INV-14, conformance 58-63). mh handles
backfill re-mines existing evidence idempotently. Routing behavior is
deliberately unchanged - the ladder that consumes this index is the
next phase.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

staging: raw conversation store and context windows (refactor phase 1.5)

Raw text now lands before the pipeline runs. add()/add_records stage
validated records into staged_records keyed by (scope, conversation,
sent_at) at enqueue time - the owner-designed layer: persist first,
then trigger. Staged rows live seven days (configurable) and purging
really deletes them, touching nothing in the evidence layer; provenance
is untouched by design.

Extraction chunks then pull budgeted context from staging: the same
conversation's tail (thread-filtered when the chunk is single-thread),
strictly older than the chunk, newest 20 records under a 4000-char
budget, deterministic order. Context records share one alias namespace
with live records and may be cited as evidence - a card resting only on
prior context is legal and fully traceable. Empty staging degrades to
the previous prompt byte-for-byte. INV-13 amended; conformance 64-67.

Verified live: an ambiguous follow-up ("changed it as discussed above,
shipping tonight") in a later flush attaches to the right matter on the
strength of staged context alone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

identity routing: the five-rung ladder (refactor phase 2)

Identity decisions leave the extraction prompt. Every accepted card now
routes through an explicit ladder: connector stamps and human
assertions above all, then exact handle hit (closed matters reachable -
a refund returns to its finished order), thread continuation, INV-5
evidence overlap - all zero-model - then one adjudication call over at
most five lexically recalled OPEN candidates carrying handles, status,
next_step, participants, and recent evidence, never title-only anchors.
The adjudication gate is strict: unoffered keys, untraceable evidence,
low confidence, or malformed output all become abstention, and
abstained cards wait in a review queue for a human instead of being
guessed onto the wall. Deterministic rungs outrank the model; every
rung and disagreement is counted, and zero_model_route_rate is now a
real eval metric (INV-15, conformance 68-73).

Checkpoint-2 eval vs the phase-0 baseline: renamed-matter over-split
eliminated by handle persistence, missed_attach zero across runs, and a
third of all routing decisions now happen without a model call.

MATTERHORN_DEV_TRACE=1 makes the service print one plain line per
received message or record - scope, conversation, sender, id, length,
and the content itself (truncated at 500 chars) - before anything is
distilled, so "what did the hub actually receive" is answerable by

hooks: --scope auto for one global Claude Code configuration

A single hooks entry in ~/.claude/settings.json can now cover every
project without collapsing them into one partition: --scope auto
resolves per project - a .matterhorn-scope file at the project root (or
any parent up to $HOME) names the scope explicitly, and projects
without one get a stable derived scope from the directory name plus a

service: dev-mode ingest trace

MATTERHORN_DEV_TRACE=1 makes the service print one plain line per
received message or record - scope, conversation, sender, id, length,
and the content itself (truncated at 500 chars) - before anything is
distilled, so "what did the hub actually receive" is answerable by
reading the log. Off by default; the trace logger bypasses the

content field. Tracing failures never break ingestion.

hooks: --scope auto for one global Claude Code configuration

A single hooks entry in ~/.claude/settings.json can now cover every
project without collapsing them into one partition: --scope auto
resolves per project - a .matterhorn-scope file at the project root (or
any parent up to $HOME) names the scope explicitly, and projects
without one get a stable derived scope from the directory name plus a
path digest, so same-named siblings never collide. Explicit --scope
values pass through untouched.

console: raw stream panel, flush deadline, update badges

conversation, sender, snippet) straight from the staging store, so
"what is arriving right now" is visible on the page, not just in
server logs. Batching gains a deadline: a scope flushes when it goes
quiet OR when its oldest pending task exceeds the max batch delay
(default five minutes), because a conversation that never goes quiet

starved exactly the busiest groups (conformance 74-75). Wall cards
show an "updated" stamp when a matter changed since the viewer last

routing: no zero-score filler candidates in adjudication

Live incident: a group started a genuinely NEW topic, lexical recall
found nothing related, the recall filled the offer with zero-scoring
matters anyway, and the adjudicator - facing a lineup of unrelated
candidates - abstained. The card queued for review, no matter formed,
and every subsequent batch on the same topic repeated the loop: seven
near-identical cards stranded in review while the wall showed nothing.

Adjudication now runs only over positively-scoring candidates; an
empty related set proceeds straight to clean new-subject creation.
Abstention is reserved for genuine ambiguity among related matters
(SPEC updated, case 71 fixture tightened). Also fixed conformance
isolation on the shared PostgreSQL database: flush_quiet is
store-global, so the runner now scopes flush reports to the case under
test - the suite passes repeatedly on a dirty shared database instead
of tripping over a neighbor case's deliberately-pending scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

extraction: progress carries the narrative, outcome only concludes

Ongoing discussions were accumulating one APPEND-forever outcome per
extraction window - the model used outcome as a per-window summary
dump, so a live topic's timeline silted up with near-identical
"discussion" outcomes. The prompt now pins the field semantics the
schema always intended: what happened in this window of an unfinished
matter goes to progress (SINGLE, supersedes), and outcome is reserved
for a conclusion, a decision reached, or a final result.

Verified live: a three-window discussion projects one matter with
rolling progress and exactly one outcome, emitted only when the
decision lands.

routing: tolerant abstain and alias evidence; batching gains a floor

The review queue flooded for two mechanical reasons, both diagnosed

routing: candidates need real lexical kinship; new is the safe default

Acceptance audit of the 111-item review queue: eight of eight sampled

engine: record change, not confirmation (change-only admission)

Every source type showed the same silt: models re-assert unchanged
values each extraction window - a matter collected status=in_progress
five times then completed three times, one email project logged nine
same-value confirmations, participants re-recorded twenty-one times.
Model-origin ASSERTs whose object_key is already live for the
predicate (SINGLE value equal, SET member present, APPEND point
identical) are now dropped at admission, counted as unchanged_dropped
in gate and task statistics. RETRACT, cleared_fields, and human-origin
assertions are exempt - a human repeating a value is an affirmation
with provenance. Timelines record change; staging keeps the dropped
evidence. Golden cases 02/27/28 updated to the intended semantics,
new cases 76-80 pin drop, change-after-drop, SET member, human
exemption, and replay identity on both backends.

Live five-window lifecycle now projects exactly two status entries
and four drops - previously five duplicates.

M0: spec first — normative SPEC.md and the golden conformance suite

The proposal calls for the specification to enter the repository before any
code, because two implementations (this Python engine and an internal Java
one) must be held to one source of truth.

- spec/SPEC.md: the nine principles (P1-P9) and ten invariants (INV-1..INV-10)
  written normatively, plus the exact assertion_id derivation, projection
  algorithm, conflict-resolution order, retract guards and query semantics.
- spec/conformance/: language-neutral golden YAML cases. Every case is also
  replayed and re-ingested by the runner, so INV-2 (idempotent replay) and
  INV-3 (projection is a pure, rebuildable function) are enforced for free on
  every case rather than tested once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M1: deterministic engine core, SQLite store, query family and CLI

Card-level ingest -> assertions -> intervals -> materialized memory cards,
with the read path deriving answers by query alone (P4/INV-10).

Design decisions worth calling out, each traceable to a production bug the
proposal records:

- INV-4 (blocker/next_step/due flicker): a field being absent means "no
  observation", never "cleared"; explicit clearing is expressed by
  EpisodeCard.cleared_fields. The condition that emits a RETRACT and the
  condition that updates the projection are one shared function, not two
  copies that can drift, and re-asserting the same value keeps the existing
  interval open instead of closing and reopening it.
- INV-5 (two unrelated matters merged into one card): merging requires an
  absolute floor of two shared sources; a single shared message is never a
  merge reason, no matter what share of the new card's evidence it represents.
- INV-8/INV-9: SINGLE conflicts resolve on (valid_from, origin, recorded_at,
  assertion_id) with human origin outranking model, and every resolved
  conflict is counted and reported rather than silently discarded.

The core carries no domain vocabulary: it executes any valid SchemaProfile,
and ships two genuinely different profiles (org-matters, personal-decisions)
so the abstraction is driven by more than one case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

M2+M3: distillation gate, protocol surfaces, adapters, PostgreSQL and release

Write path (the only place a model is allowed to run, P1):
- LlmGateway SPI (OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / null) behind an async dream
  queue. ingest() never calls a model; dream() drains the queue and re-projects
  inside one transaction (INV-6).
- A validation gate with named, counted rejection reasons (P3). The load-bearing
  one is SOURCE_NOT_TRACEABLE: a candidate's cited sources must be a subset of
  the originating card's evidence, so the model cannot invent provenance. The
  same traceability check backs the message->card adapter — one implementation,
  not two.
- Gated creation of non-primary child subjects, which is what makes the
  flagship profile's one semantic predicate (decision_adopted on DECISION_SLOT)
  reachable at all. Child keys are derived deterministically, so a replayed
  dream creates no duplicate subject.

Read path: MCP server on the official SDK (seven tools), FastAPI REST 1:1 with
those tools, and a Claude Skill. All three share one service layer, and none of
them can reach the distill package — enforced by an import-graph test.

Storage: a second backend. PostgreSQL exists to prove the spec is implementable
twice, so the entire conformance suite runs against both, and ordering is
pinned to bytewise (COLLATE "C" / BINARY) rather than the server's locale — a
spec whose answers depend on a deployment's collation is not a spec.

Release: adapters for ReMe/OpenViking digests, four runnable examples including
the human-correction flow, Docker, docs, and CI with the cross-backend
conformance suite as a required gate against the two implementations drifting.

Verified: 138 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17, on both C and
en_US.UTF-8 collations; mh conformance run passes 37/37 on both backends and
exits non-zero on a seeded failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cli): honest exit-code contract and a terminal correction path

Both defects were masked by a fabricated dependency: a previous build could not
download Typer and installed a 103-line hand-written stub into the venv under
the name `typer 0.0.0+verification`. Every CLI test had been passing against
that stub. The venv has been rebuilt with real Typer 0.27.0, which is how these
surfaced.

- `mh conformance run` now exits 0 when all cases pass, 1 when cases run and
  some fail, and 2 when the suite itself is unusable. It previously raised
  click.exceptions.Exit(2), which the stub honoured and real Typer does not, so
  an unreadable suite exited 1 with a traceback. This command is the CI gate and
  the harness the internal Java implementation mirrors, so its exit contract is
  part of the deliverable, not an implementation detail.
- `mh correct` closes the one surface where the correction protocol was missing.
  P8 makes corrections a first-class part of the core contract and the proposal
  names an unused correction protocol as a top risk, yet an operator at a
  terminal had no way to file one.
- Typer and click now carry lower bounds so a fresh install cannot silently
  pick up an incompatible version.

Verified: 141 tests green across SQLite and PostgreSQL 17; the three exit codes
demonstrated for real; a correction through the CLI flips a query answer from
(blocked, model) to (open, human).
